questions.question: How many unique colors will be required for proper vertex coloring of a complete graph having n vertices?

explanations.a: Incorrect. A graph cannot be colored with 0 colors as each vertex must be assigned at least one color.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A complete graph cannot be colored with just 1 color as all vertices are connected to each other and must have different colors.
explanations.c: Correct! In a complete graph, every vertex is connected to every other vertex, so each vertex must have a unique color, requiring exactly n colors.
explanations.d: Incorrect. While n! represents the number of possible different arrangements of n colors, the minimum number of colors needed is just n.

questions.question: In the context of the Four Color Theorem mentioned in map coloring, what is the maximum number of colors needed to color any planar map?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Two colors are insufficient for many planar maps, especially those with triangular regions.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Three colors are not always sufficient for all planar maps.
explanations.c: Correct! The Four Color Theorem states that any planar map can be colored with at most 4 colors such that no two adjacent regions have the same color.
explanations.d: Incorrect. While 5 colors would work, the Four Color Theorem proves that 4 colors are always sufficient.

questions.question: What is the chromatic number of a tree with n vertices (where n > 1)?

explanations.a: Incorrect. A tree with more than 1 vertex has edges, so it requires at least 2 colors.
explanations.b: Correct! A tree is a connected acyclic graph and is bipartite, so it can always be colored with exactly 2 colors by alternating colors along any path.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Two colors are always sufficient for any tree structure.
explanations.d: Incorrect. While n colors would work, it's excessive - only 2 colors are needed for trees.

questions.question: A bipartite graph can always be properly vertex-coloured with

answers.b: The number of colours equal to the degree of any vertex.
answers.d: The number of colours equal to the number of vertices in one partition.

explanations.a: Incorrect. While you can use more colors, a bipartite graph has a specific minimum number of colors needed.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The degree of vertices is not directly related to the chromatic number of a bipartite graph.
explanations.c: Correct! A bipartite graph can always be colored with exactly 2 colors because its vertices can be divided into two independent sets with no edges within each set.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The number of vertices in a partition is not related to the chromatic number of a bipartite graph.

questions.question: Which graph coloring application is used when assigning frequencies to mobile towers to avoid interference?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Map coloring is used for geographical regions, not frequency assignment.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Sudoku is a different application of graph coloring principles.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Exam scheduling uses graph coloring but for academic scheduling, not frequency assignment.
explanations.d: Correct! Mobile radio frequency assignment uses graph coloring where towers are vertices and edges connect towers in range of each other, ensuring adjacent towers get different frequencies.

questions.question: What is the chromatic number of a cycle graph with n vertices where n is odd?

explanations.a: Incorrect. A cycle graph cannot be colored with just 1 color as adjacent vertices must have different colors.
explanations.b: Incorrect. An odd cycle cannot be colored with 2 colors as it's not bipartite.
explanations.c: Correct! Any odd cycle requires exactly 3 colors for proper vertex coloring, as it cannot be colored with 2 colors but can always be colored with 3.
explanations.d: Incorrect. While n colors would work, it's excessive - 3 colors are sufficient for any cycle graph regardless of size.
